summary: The study describes the synthesis of CeO2/TiO2 core-shell inverse opals using atomic layer deposition (ALD) to tailor pore size and architecture. The ALD process was carried out at 90 8C using TDMAT and water as precursors. The resulting materials showed enhanced photocatalytic activity under UVA irradiation, making them suitable for applications in wastewater purification and photonic-bandgap materials.
evidence: The deposition process was carried out at low temperature (90 8C) for several reasons. Firstly, this temperature is high enough to allow the ALD process to occur under self-limiting conditions, thus giving rise to highly conformal and reproducible films. The TiO2 deposition was very uniform over the whole sample and occurred in a conformal way, which allowed retention of the microstructural order that was originally determined by the underlying inverse opal scaffold.
